children: U.S. law firm Barnes & Thornburg has sued former NBA basketball player Luol Deng for more than $1 million, alleging the one-time Chicago Bulls All-Star hired the firm for legal work on a series of real estate deals and never paid his bills.

Barnes & Thornburg filed the lawsuit on August 26 in Cook County Circuit Court, alleging breach of contract and other claims. It said Deng hired the firm to handle the refinancing of a New York-based property, as well as negotiating with lenders, exploring financial options and restructuring loans on a Chicago-based property.
The firm said it is seeking more than $1.05 million in legal fees plus interest.
The lawsuit said Deng has not made any payments "despite repeated efforts" by Barnes & Thornburg's attorneys to obtain payment from him.

Deng played in the NBA for 15 years, including a 10-year stint on the Chicago Bulls. He currently serves as president of the South Sudan Basketball Federation (SSBF), a position he has held since 2019. The South Sudan men's team, also known as the "Bright Stars," made its Olympic debut in 2024.
A lawyer for Deng and spokespersons for SSBF and Barnes & Thornburg did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
